display.text: A single cell's value of (observed − expected)²/expected in the overall χ² statistic; large contributions identify cells with substantial discrepancies.
Family of nonnegative distributions indexed by degrees of freedom, used to approximate the null distribution of the independence-test statistic when conditions hold.
Sum over cells of (observed − expected)²/expected; larger values indicate greater disagreement with independence. Notation: χ².
Test of whether two categorical variables are associated in a population, comparing observed cell counts with counts expected under independence. Also called χ² test.
Number (r − 1)(c − 1) used for the chi-square reference distribution of a table with r rows and c columns, excluding totals.

response.correctResponse: degrees of freedom for a contingency table

display.text: Count predicted for a cell under independence, calculated as its row total times its column total divided by the table total. Also called expected frequency.
Requirement for adequate cell sizes in the chi-square approximation. The text gives all expected counts above 1 with at least 80% above 5, or the more conservative rule that all exceed 5.
Absence of association: the distribution of one variable is the same across categories of the other; this is the chi-square test's null hypothesis.
Number of sampled observations actually falling in a particular cell of a contingency table. Also called observed frequency.
Probability under independence of obtaining a χ² statistic at least as large as the observed value; it is an upper-tail probability.
